title: Pilot Technical Handshake — Mini Deck (sketch)
content:
Purpose: one-page compact deck to guide a cross-functional pilot kickoff between Sales/SE, Platform, and SRE. Goal: reduce friction during first 30 days, make the technical handoff deterministic, and give SEs scripts for fallbacks and customer conversations.

Slide 1 — Why this exists
- Common failure mode: pilot gets stuck on infra/latency unknowns or billing/discovery mismatch.
- Outcome we want: predictable first 72h smoke test, 7-day evidence of viability, and go/no-go checklist for Reserved/Dedicated ask.
- Speaker note: emphasize reducing time-to-evidence, not convincing on features.

Slide 2 — Quick roles & commitments (30s)
- SE (sales engineer): owns customer expectations, integration sandbox, demo prompts.
- Platform engineer: provisioning, routing policy, model variant mapping for pilot.
- SRE/ops: SLA monitoring, canary hooks, incident contact.
- Customer technical lead: test data, auth scope, network contact.

Slide 3 — Pilot types we support (pick one)
- Smoke pilot (2–3 days): validate latency, auth, and simple prompt set.
- Feature pilot (7–14 days): integration with app flow, token cost sanity checks, basic quality metrics.
- Scale proof (30 days): throughput, caching effectiveness, RU/commit ask.

Slide 4 — 72-hour smoke checklist (copyable)
- Pre-kick: API keys provisioned + test account created.
- Day 0: deploy model variant (v1-lite) to dev pool; run 50 synthetic calls at expected P95 prompt length.
- Day 1: integrate app endpoint + run end-to-end sample flows (10 users).
- Day 2: observe cost-per-1k-tokens estimate, log latency p50/p95, validate output quality on 20 QA prompts.
- Acceptance: p95 latency within agreed SLO or documented fallback engaged.

Speaker note: include quick curl examples for SE to paste into customer Slack. TODO: add cURL snippets and SDK one-liners (low priority).

Slide 5 — Fallback and graceful degradation play (script for SE)
- If p95 > target: route to lower-capacity model variant (quantized) + inform customer: "temporary degrade to preserve responsiveness; quality delta monitored".
- If rate limits hit: enable burst capacity for X minutes (billing note), schedule scaling window.
- If errors spike: switch routing policy to hosted fallback region and open incident channel.
- Copyable customer message included at bottom.

Slide 6 — Quick economics heuristic (for deal conversations)
- Rule of thumb: 1M tokens gen ~= $X on hosted small model, $~0.6X on dedicated with caching turned on for prefix-heavy workloads. (Placeholder numbers; fill with actual pricing).
- SE tip: show a 30-day projection with and without KV caching — demonstrate 20–60% delta depending on prompt reuse.

Slide 7 — Observability & SLOs to track during pilot
- Latency distribution (p50/p95/p99), error rate, token/sec per customer, KV cache hit ratio, cost per 1k tokens.
- Which dashboards to watch: Quick links to pilot dashboard (Confluence link), alert thresholds to set (example: error rate >0.5% over 5m).

Slide 8 — Canary checklist for small rollouts (example script)
- Canary cohort: 5% of traffic, 1 region, 48 hours.
- Metrics: compare latency, errors, quality regressions vs baseline.
- Abort conditions: sustained p95 increase >30% or quality drop >5% on evaluated prompt set.

Slide 9 — Short customer conversation scripts (exports for SEs)
- When to push for Dedicated: "we're seeing consistent traffic X with cache-hit <Y and cost projection above your threshold".
- When to request Private: "data residency + audit trail requirements triggered by regulator X".
- Handshake line: "We'll run a 72-hour smoke, you sign off on acceptance criteria, then we schedule scale steps."

Slide 10 — Example pilot vignette (toy numbers)
- Customer: docs-search app, 3k monthly active users, avg prompt length 140 tokens.
- Baseline (hosted): p95=220ms, cost ~ $2.4k/month; with prefix caching on Dedicated: p95=140ms, cost ~$1.6k/month (est.).
- Bottom line: show both performance and cost delta so buyer can justify commit.

Slide 11 — Open questions & risks (for internal discussion)
- API quota bumps: who approves bursts > $Y? (sales ops question).
- Heavy long-sequence workloads: define 'long' and draft recommended model variants.
- Security: when do we require VPC/Private vs token-scoped hosted usage?
- TODO: map these to policy owners and add dates.

Slide 12 — Next steps checklist for SE after pilot sign-off
- Produce 1-pg pilot summary: metrics, logs, decision (go->reserved/dedicated / no-go->follow-up).
- Handoff ticket to Account Exec + Solutions Eng + Billing ops. Attach audit logs and cost projection.

Appendix — Copy-paste assets (placeholders)
- Slack-ready messages for latency incidents (short and long form).
- SE one-liners for procurement and legal.
- Demo prompt library: 6 prompts to validate hallucination/regression.

Notes to self (draft style)
- Keep this under 12 slides for an email deck.
- Need input from pricing on actual $ numbers (ping: @finance-pricing).
- Add cURL snippets and SDK copy for immediate use in customer calls.
- Validate canary abort thresholds with SRE (Rohit).

References and links (internal)
- Confluence sketch: https://confluence.redwoodai/internal/PILOT-HANDSHAKE-117
- Jira for pilot automation work: JIRA-4562
- Demo script PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/pilot-scripts/pull/89

End of deck — this is intentionally a working sketch. Feedback requested from SEs and Platform before we finalize and convert to polished slides.
